طَلِيلٌ : see مَطْلُولٌ. ＝
-A2- Also Sweet; syn. حُلْوٌ: (so accord. to the O and some copies of the K: accord. to other copies of the K, i. q. خِلق; i. e., accord. to some of these copies, خَلْقٌ; accord. to some, خَلَقٌ; and accord. to some, خَلِقٌ:) thus expl. by Ibn-'Abbád; and said by him to be of the dial. of Hudheyl. (O.) [The explanation in the O is, I doubt not, the right: and hence] ―
-b2- طَلِيلَةٌ applied to a خُطْبَة: see طَلٌّ, latter part. ＝
-A3- Also A mat; syn. حَصِيرٌ: (IAar, O, K:) or such as is woven of [the leaves of the] دَوْم [or Theban palm-tree]; or of the leaves of the date-palm; or of the قُشُور [app. meaning the peels of the branches] thereof: (K, TA:) so in the M: in the T it is said that ↓ طَلِيلَةٌ means, accord. to AA, a [mat of the kind called] بُورِيَآء; and accord. to As, a بَارِىّ [which signifies the same as بوريآ]: (TA:) pl. أَطِلَّةٌ and طِلَّةٌ and طُلُلٌ. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
